answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. What survives to the ocean is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. A zephyr of per-task receipts records who did what, and the trellis of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, diluted when peers disagree, rewards vest against future work.
